original_question: Let X be an ordered Banach space. If every weakly convergent increasing net in X is norm convergent, must the cone X+ be normal?
target_in_paper: Conjecture 1.1 in Section 1: the paper's converse-to-Dini question, asking whether Dini's theorem on an ordered Banach space forces the positive cone to be normal. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.19768?utm_source=openai))
correct_elements: Your draft gets the core mathematical content right: the ambient setting is an ordered Banach space, the hypothesis concerns increasing weakly convergent monotone objects, the conclusion is norm convergence, and the desired consequence is normality of the cone X_+. This is clearly aimed at the paper's Dini-theorem/normal-cone problem. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.19768?utm_source=openai))
missing_details: The paper's target is sequence-based Dini theory, not arbitrary nets: the nearby main evidence in Theorem 1.3 is that a reflexive ordered Banach space with non-normal cone always contains an increasing sequence that converges weakly but not in norm, so your net version is slightly broader than the paper's official scope. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.19768?utm_source=openai))

To be stand-alone, the order should be tied explicitly to the cone X_+, so 'increasing' means x_n <= x_{n+1} with respect to the order induced by X_+. ([link.springer.com](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s00028-024-01044-8?utm_source=openai))

The paper frames the hypothesis as 'Dini's theorem holds on X', i.e. every increasing weakly convergent sequence in X converges in norm; using that label keeps the question closest to the paper's intent. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.19768?utm_source=openai))

For full faithfulness to the paper's ordered-space setup, one should specify that X is a real ordered Banach space with closed positive cone X_+. ([link.springer.com](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s00028-024-01044-8?utm_source=openai))

The nearby context matters: Theorem 1.3 proves the conjectural converse in the reflexive case, so the sharp paper-faithful question is precisely whether that converse remains true without reflexivity. ([sciencedirect.com](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0022247X25004755?utm_source=openai))
refined_question: Let X be a real ordered Banach space with closed positive cone X_+. Assume that Dini's theorem holds on X, in the sense that every increasing weakly convergent sequence in X converges in norm. Must the cone X_+ be normal? ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.19768?utm_source=openai))
equivalent_formulation: Equivalently, if every increasing sequence (x_n) in X that converges weakly to some x in X automatically satisfies ||x_n - x|| -> 0, does it follow that X_+ is normal? ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.19768?utm_source=openai))
justification: The draft is aiming at the introduction's converse-to-Dini conjecture, not at the neighboring Levi-property questions. The abstract identifies one of the paper's main results as the reflexive-case obstruction: if X is reflexive and X_+ is non-normal, then one can find an increasing sequence that converges weakly but not in norm. That is exactly the evidence one cites for a conjecture asking whether Dini's theorem characterizes normality of the cone in general. Hence the paper-faithful refinement should use the sequence-based Dini formulation, rather than the broader net formulation in the draft. ([sciencedirect.com](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0022247X25004755?utm_source=openai))
